descriptionChirho: To bring or lead a person down from one place to another, especially escorting someone down to a lower location or before an authority — used of bringing Paul down to Caesarea (Acts 9:30; 23:15, 20, 28) and before the Sanhedrin (Acts 22:30); also bringing boats to shore (Luke 5:11) and bringing Christ down (Rom 10:6).

labelChirho: land / put in to shore (nautical, intransitive)
descriptionChirho: Nautical technical term in passive/intransitive use for a ship coming to land or putting in at a port — 'we landed at Sidon' (Acts 27:3); 'having landed at Syracuse' (Acts 28:12).
